newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- cash down, new issues firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- cash down, new issues firm.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds ended down 1/4 point as a cascade of firmly priced new issues all but eclipsed secondary market action.
"It's like all of 1996," one trader said. "People care about new issues and they don't care about what's in the secondary."

A municipal analyst described new issue pricing as "firm," and said Connecticut's $150 million general obligation bonds came in especially strong. Smith Barney Inc won the deal at 5.2778 percent TIC. Bonds were reoffered to investors at a top yield of 5.55 percent in 2017, and the account was closed by Tuesday afternoon.
Merrill Lynch & Co won the day's biggest deal--$556 million Pennsylvania GOs--at a true interest cost of 5.21 percent.

Bonds were reoffered to investors at a top yield of 5.4 percent in 2012, while bonds in the top maturity of 2017 were not formally reoffered. A $117 million balance was reported on the deal by day's end.
On the negotiated side, Lehman Brothers said it repriced $190 million Houston, Texas, Airport System revenue bonds, cutting the yield in 2017 to 5.882 percent from 5.926 percent.
Goldman Sachs & Co said it restructured a $160 million California Housing Finance Agency offering. The deal featured a top tax-exempt yield of yield of 6.05 percent in 2028.
Bear Stearns & Co said it repriced and restructured $123 million New York Mortgage Agency bonds, raising the top yield in 2027 to 6.125 percent from 6.10 percent.

In the secondary market, much of the buzz centered on a large list from a single customer. The $220 million to $250 million list -- which two traders said came from Putnam -- received some good bids, they said.
"I think they traded the whole list, and a fair amount of it went away," one trader said.

Overall, secondary muni cash closed down 1/4 point, a municipal analyst said. High-grade issues worsened by two basis points in the long end, while dollar bonds closed down 1/4 to 3/8 of a point, mainly on quotes.

Dollars bonds opened flat, but sank 1/4 to 3/8 of a point by noon (EST). Bonds rebounded to be down just 1/8 to 1/4 point by early afternoon, but weakened again going into the close, the analyst said.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed down 7/32 at 113-23/32. The June T-bond contract closed down 4/32 at 110. The MOB spread was 119 ticks.
In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 14/32 at 97-3/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
